name: Thighmaster-era Thigh Gym

lead: The Thigh Gym belongs to the family of squeeze-between-the-knees exercisers popularised in the 1990s, best known through the ThighMaster. It resists the squeezing motion of the inner thighs (hip adductors) and is used to tone that area.
Users wanting firmer-looking legs used it at home, often while doing something else. Little formal research on the devices exists, and the product remains mainly a nostalgia item.

paras: The device sits between the knees or thighs and is squeezed repeatedly. Its spring or bent-tube resistance is fixed and small compared with gym machines, so it is typically combined with other leg training.
Low risk for most users. Muscle soreness or strain is possible if overdone.

angle.text: The device gives light resistance to the inner thigh muscles. People use it for a toned look in the legs, usually alongside general exercise.

lead: The Thigh Gym is a spring-loaded squeeze exerciser of the type that spread during the 1990s fitness infomercial boom, best known through the ThighMaster [1]. The ThighMaster is two bent metal tubes joined by a hinge, placed between the knees and squeezed to work the hip adductors [1].

The ThighMaster originated as a physical-therapy device called the V-Bar, created by Swedish medical intern Anne Marie Bennstrom (Prescott), and was marketed by Joshua Reynolds with actress Suzanne Somers in 1990s infomercials that showed people exercising while watching television [1].
Used for appearance, such devices aim at toned inner thighs. The wiki already has a dedicated ThighMaster entry; this one covers the wider 1990s generation of similar products.

paras: Squeeze devices use a hinge, spring or bent tube to resist the knees being pressed together, and can also be used for arms and other muscle groups [1].
